issues.description: The problem statement's prose (line listing attributes) refers to attributes as 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents', while the UML diagram and the tests expect attributes named 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents'. This naming inconsistency can confuse students about the exact attribute names to implement and the constructor parameter order they are asked to follow.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute naming consistent across the problem text, UML, template, and tests. Update the prose that lists attributes to use 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' (to match the UML and tests), or alternatively adjust the UML and tests to use 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents'. Also update the template TODO comments to reference the exact attribute names students should implement.

issues.description: The problem statement prose refers to the student-count attributes as "inscribedStudents" and "guestStudents" while the UML and the solution implementation use the names "numberOfInscribedStudents" and "numberOfGuestStudents". This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual attributes (total counts of inscribed and guest students) can create minor mapping confusion: students reading the prose might look for fields named exactly as in the text, whereas the expected/implemented fields include the "numberOf" prefix.
issues.suggestedFix: Use consistent identifiers across all artifacts. Update the problem statement prose to use the same attribute names as the UML and solution (e.g. "numberOfInscribedStudents" and "numberOfGuestStudents"), or alternatively rename the UML and solution attributes to match the prose ("inscribedStudents" and "guestStudents"). Prefer keeping the explicit "numberOf..." names to match test and method names (e.g. getNumberOfInscribedStudents()).
